mainTopic: Witnesses for עדות אשה, when a judge may marry a woman whose case he handled, and whether a forbidden marriage must be undone
overview: The גמרא finishes discussing רב מנשה's rule that a גזלן by rabbinic law may testify that a woman's husband died, but a גזלן by Torah law may not. It shows two ways to read the רבנן of the משנה. In the first, following רבא, a man who says 'I killed him' is not counted as a רשע, so רב מנשה fits the רבנן. In the second, עדות אשה is lenient even for a real רשע, so רב יוסף fits the רבנן and רב מנשה follows רבי יהודה. רב יהודה then explains that 'We killed him' means 'I was with his killers', and a ברייתא about a bandit backs this up. A new משנה rules that a חכם who left a woman forbidden through her נדר may not marry her, but a judge at her מיאון or חליצה may, since he sat on a court. The גמרא explains that the חכם must be a single expert, and that the word 'court' teaches that מיאון needs three judges. Finally, רב כהנא and רב אשי disagree about whether a man who married a woman forbidden to him must divorce her. רב אשי begins to prove his view from a משנה, and his proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב מנשה: a rabbinic robber may testify for a woman, a Torah robber may not
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשה rules that a גזלן whose robbery is only rabbinic is still kosher for עדות אשה, but a גזלן by Torah law is פסול even for עדות אשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A robber by rabbinic law is fit to testify that a woman's husband died. A robber by Torah law is unfit for this testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states רב מנשה's rule about which kind of robber may testify that a woman's husband died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rabbinic-level גזלן is normally barred from testimony, but here he is allowed because עדות אשה is more lenient. A Torah-level גזלן is a real רשע, and even this leniency does not help him.

keyTerms.meaning: A robber, who is normally disqualified as a witness
By their words, meaning by rabbinic law
Testimony that a woman's husband died, so she may remarry
Fit / unfit to serve as a witness

phrases.english: A robber by rabbinic law
is fit for a woman's testimony,
a robber by Torah law
is unfit for a woman's testimony.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב מנשה's statement from the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rabbinic-level גזלן may testify for an אשה; a Torah-level גזלן may not.

steps.title: Does רב מנשה follow only רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב מנשה's rule matches only רבי יהודה in the משנה, who disqualifies someone who says 'I killed him'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב מנשה spoke according to רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רב מנשה's rule fits only the view of רבי יהודה. This sets up the next move, where רב מנשה defends himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the רבנן accept even someone who says 'I killed him', who is a Torah-level רשע. רבי יהודה rejects him. Since רב מנשה rejects a Torah-level רשע, he seems to agree only with רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? Opens a suggestion the גמרא will test
In line with the view of רבי יהודה

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Menashe
spoke according to Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: In our משנה, רבי יהודה does not accept a witness who says 'I killed him'.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא רַב מְנַשֶּׁה דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב מנשה's rule against the dispute in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רב מנשה's rule limited to רבי יהודה's view, against the רבנן?

steps.title: רב מנשה fits the רבנן too, using רבא's principle
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשה can say he agrees even with the רבנן. They accept 'I killed him' because, as רבא says, a person cannot make himself a רשע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשה can tell you: I meant even according to the רבנן. The reason of the רבנן here is like רבא, who said: a person is his own relative, and a person cannot make himself wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב מנשה's rule also fits the רבנן, because the person saying 'I killed him' never actually becomes a רשע in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבא's rule, a person is like a relative to himself, so his words about his own guilt are not accepted. The court ignores the 'I killed' part and accepts only 'he is dead'. So he is not a real Torah-level רשע, and the רבנן never accepted a true Torah-level רשע.

keyTerms.meaning: A person is a relative to himself, so he cannot testify about himself
A person cannot make himself wicked by his own testimony

steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's rule lets the court split a statement: it ignores the self-incriminating part and accepts the rest.

phrases.english: Rav Menashe can say to you:
I spoke even according to the Rabbis —
and the Rabbis' reason here is like Rava,
as Rava said:
a person is his own relative,
phrases.notes: Just as a relative can't testify, a person can't testify about himself.

phrases.english: and a person does not make himself wicked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב מְנַשֶּׁה אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion that רב מנשה follows only רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the reason of the רבנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן accept a self-admitted murderer, so they would accept a Torah-level רשע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן accept him only because his self-admission is ignored, so he never becomes a רשע.

steps.title: Then does רב יוסף follow only רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: If the רבנן's reason is רבא's rule, then רב יוסף, who disagrees with רבא, seems to fit only רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב יוסף spoke according to רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the question onto רב יוסף, who disagreed with רבא. This sets up רב יוסף's defense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף holds that a person's statement about himself is accepted, so he can make himself a רשע. If so, someone who says 'I killed him' really is a רשע, and the רבנן's acceptance of him would not make sense. So רב יוסף seems to match only רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? Same as נֵימָא
The אמורא who disagreed with רבא about testifying against oneself

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Yosef
phrases.notes: רב יוסף earlier ruled that a man's testimony about his own sin counts against him, which is the opposite of רבא.

phrases.english: spoke according to Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the previous answer, which tied the רבנן to רבא, against רב יוסף.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רב יוסף's view limited to רבי יהודה, since he rejects רבא's principle?

steps.title: רב יוסף fits the Rabbis because a woman's testimony is lenient
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף can say he agrees even with the רבנן, because they were lenient with עדות אשה and accept even a רשע. According to this, it is רב מנשה who follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף can tell you: I meant even according to the רבנן, because a woman's testimony is different, since the רבנן were lenient with it. And רב מנשה spoke according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב יוסף fits the רבנן because, for עדות אשה, they accept even a real רשע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the רבנן's reason is not רבא's rule but a special leniency for עדות אשה. With this reading, the רבנן accept even a Torah-level רשע. So רב מנשה, who rejects a Torah-level רשע, must follow רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to read the רבנן: (1) like רבא, the self-admitted killer is not a רשע, so רב מנשה fits the רבנן; (2) עדות אשה is lenient even for a רשע, so רב יוסף fits the רבנן and רב מנשה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: The two answers cannot both fit the רבנן together. Whoever fits the רבנן in one answer, the other must follow רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef can say to you:
I spoke even according to the Rabbis,
and a woman's testimony is different,
since the Rabbis were lenient with it.
And Rav Menashe spoke according to Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב יוֹסֵף אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on רב יוסף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason for the רבנן: special leniency for עדות אשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף must follow רבי יהודה, since he holds a person can make himself a רשע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן accept even a רשע for עדות אשה, so רב יוסף fits them; רב מנשה then follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה treat 'I killed him' and 'We killed him' differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks why רבי יהודה rejects 'I killed him' but accepts 'We killed him'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I killed him' etc., 'We killed him', she may marry etc. What is the difference between 'I killed him' and 'We killed him'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the words of the משנה and asks about רבי יהודה's distinction. This sets up רב יהודה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'We killed him' seems to include the speaker among the killers. So he should be a רשע just like the one who says 'I killed him'. Why should רבי יהודה accept him?

phrases.english: 'I killed him' etc., 'We killed him', she may marry etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה, where רבי יהודה rejects 'I killed him' but allows 'We killed him'.

phrases.english: What is different about 'I killed him'
and what is different about 'We killed him'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הֲרַגְתִּיו וּמַאי שְׁנָא הֲרַגְנוּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is 'We killed him' accepted by רבי יהודה if the speaker is also a killer?

steps.title: 'We killed him' means 'I was with his killers'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that 'We killed him' refers to someone who says he was only present with the killers, not that he killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is where he says, 'I was with his killers.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that the 'We killed him' witness only claims he was among the killers, without taking part himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being present is not the same as murdering, so this witness is not a Torah-level רשע. That is why רבי יהודה accepts him, while the one who says 'I killed him' admits to murder.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where he says

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, 'I killed him' makes the witness a murderer, but 'We killed him' means he was only with the killers, so he may testify.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
phrases.notes: This is רב יהודה the אמורא, not רבי יהודה from the משנה.

phrases.english: Where he says: I was with his killers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּאוֹמֵר אֲנִי הָיִיתִי עִם הוֹרְגָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'We killed him' means the witness was only present with the killers and did not kill.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the bandit who confessed to killing שמעון בן כהן
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים tell רבי יהודה about a bandit about to be executed who said he killed שמעון בן כהן. Based on that, they let the wife remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: They said to רבי יהודה: A bandit was being taken to be executed in the passage of Cappadocia. He said: 'Go tell the wife of שמעון בן כהן that I killed her husband as I entered Lod' (some say: 'as he entered Lod'). And they let his wife remarry!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which the חכמים challenge רבי יהודה with a real story. This sets up the next step, where רבי יהודה's reply will support רב יהודה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story seems to show that even someone who says 'I killed him' is believed for עדות אשה, which is against רבי יהודה. The גמרא brings it because רבי יהודה's answer will match exactly what רב יהודה said in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And it is taught:
They said to Rabbi Yehuda:
There was an incident with a certain armed bandit
who was taken out to be executed
in the passage of Cappadocia,
and he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: ״לְכוּ אִמְרוּ לָהּ לְאֵשֶׁת שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן כֹּהֵן:
phrases.english: "Go and tell the wife of Shimon the Kohen:
'I killed her husband
as I entered Lod.'"
And some say: 'as he entered Lod,'
and they let his wife remarry!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to back up רב יהודה's explanation of 'We killed him'.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's claim that רבי יהודה accepts a witness only when he says he was with the killers
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the bandit and the wife of Shimon the Kohen

steps.title: רבי יהודה: he only said he was with the killers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rejects the proof. The bandit only said he was present with the killers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: You bring a proof from there?! It was a case where he said: 'I was with his killers.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה pushes back on the חכמים's story. He says the bandit never claimed he did the killing himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the reading רב יהודה gave in step 7: the witness was there but did not kill. Because רבי יהודה himself says it, רב יהודה's explanation is now supported by a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? (rejecting the evidence)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, a witness who says 'I was with the killers' is believed, but one who says 'I killed him' is not.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Is there a proof from there?!
It was a case where he said:
"I was with his killers."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה's answer inside the ברייתא, which matches רב יהודה's explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The חכמים's proof from the story
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The bandit never said he killed the husband. He said he was with the killers.

steps.title: But he is called a bandit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה's reading: the ברייתא calls him a bandit, so he must have been a killer.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches that he was a 'bandit'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יהודה's reading. If the man is called a bandit, it sounds like he was a violent person who killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he was a known killer, then 'I was with his killers' sounds like a cover for 'I killed him'. That would make him a רשע, and רבי יהודה should not believe him.

phrases.english: But it teaches "an armed bandit"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's reading of the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that the bandit only said he was present
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'bandit' suggests he was himself a killer, so he is a רשע.

steps.title: He was only arrested on a banditry charge
steps.stepSummary: Being called a bandit only means he was arrested for banditry, not that he killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was caught on a charge of banditry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'bandit' just describes what he was arrested for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being caught for banditry does not prove he personally killed anyone. So he can still be someone who was only with the killers.

phrases.english: He was caught on a charge of banditry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the word 'bandit'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a word in the source
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Bandit' only means he was arrested for banditry.

steps.title: But he was taken out to be executed
steps.stepSummary: If he was being executed, he must have been found guilty of murder.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches that he 'went out to be executed'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks again. Execution sounds like he was convicted of killing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Robbery alone would not normally carry a death sentence. So the death sentence suggests he was a murderer, which brings back the problem that he is a רשע.

phrases.english: But it teaches "he was taken out" to be executed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רבי יהודה's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that he was only arrested for banditry
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A death sentence implies a murder conviction.

steps.title: A non-Jewish court executes without checking carefully
steps.stepSummary: It was a non-Jewish court, which executes gang members without checking who actually killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a non-Jewish court, which does not check carefully, and executes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the death sentence proves nothing, because this court was not careful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-Jewish court would execute anyone in a gang of bandits, whether or not he killed. So the bandit may truly have only been with the killers, and the ברייתא still supports רבי יהודה as רב יהודה explained him.
steps.whatToRemember: The bandit story fits רבי יהודה: the man only said he was with the killers. The words 'bandit' and 'executed' do not prove he killed.

phrases.english: It was a non-Jewish court,
which does not check carefully, and executes.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּי דִינָא דְּגוֹיִם, דְּלָא דָּיְיקִי וְקָטְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the death sentence and closes the discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the setting of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The death sentence shows he was a convicted murderer.
steps.terutzMaskana: A non-Jewish court executes every gang member without checking, so the sentence proves nothing.

steps.title: New משנה: when a חכם or judge may marry the woman
steps.stepSummary: A חכם who left a woman forbidden to her husband through a נדר may not marry her. A judge before whom she did מיאון or חליצה may marry her, because he was one of a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A חכם who left a woman forbidden to her husband by a נדר may not marry her. If she did מיאון, or did חליצה in front of him, he may marry her, because he is part of a בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It is about whether a חכם or judge who handled a woman's case may marry her afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the נדר, people might suspect he kept her forbidden to her husband so he could marry her himself. With מיאון and חליצה, he was only one judge on a court, so there is no such suspicion.

keyTerms.meaning: She did מיאון: a girl married off as a minor refuses the marriage
She did חליצה, the ceremony that frees a widow from יבום

steps.confusionAlert: The חכם did not make the woman's נדר. She made it. He refused to undo it, so it stayed in force.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
A Sage who rendered the woman forbidden
phrases.notes: He didn't make her vow. He refused to undo it, so she stayed forbidden.

phrases.english: to her husband through a vow
may not marry her.
If she did refusal, or did chalitza before him,
he may marry her,
because he is a court.
phrases.notes: He means he was one judge on a court with others, so the decision was not his alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶחָכָם שֶׁאָסַר אֶת הָאִשָּׁה בְּנֶדֶר עַל בַּעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חכם who left a woman forbidden by a נדר may not marry her. A judge at her מיאון or חליצה may marry her, because he was part of a בית דין.

steps.title: Inference: if he permitted her, he may marry her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from the משנה that if the חכם undid the נדר, he may marry her later.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This implies that if he permitted her, he may marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an inference from the משנה's wording. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only forbids him when he forbade her. So if he permitted her to her husband, and she later became free to marry, he may marry her. The גמרא will now ask what kind of judge this must be.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
This implies: if he permitted her,
he may marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה's first case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the חכם undid the נדר, he may later marry the woman.

steps.title: What case is this? Maybe a single judge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the משנה means, and suggests a single judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say a single judge...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of judge undid the נדר. It first tries the idea of a single judge, setting up a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks of one חכם, which sounds like he acted alone. The גמרא tests whether that can work.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If you say with a single judge,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case the inference refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חכם in the משנה is a single judge or part of a court

steps.title: A single judge cannot undo vows; it takes three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that one judge cannot undo vows, since a ברייתא says undoing vows needs three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can a single judge undo vows? But רבי חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב עמרם that a ברייתא taught: undoing vows needs three!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea of a single judge. It quotes a ברייתא that undoing vows needs three judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If undoing vows needs three judges, then a single חכם could not have handled her נדר by himself, so the one-judge reading seems impossible. The גמרא next tries three judges (step 18) and finally answers in step 20 with a single expert.

phrases.english: Can a single judge dissolve vows?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר (רַב אָמַר) רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: But didn't (Rav say that) Rabbi Chiya bar Avin say
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't. The teaching is the same either way.

phrases.english: that Rav Amram said: It was taught:
Dissolving vows requires three!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion that the חכם was a single judge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה's חכם acted alone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says undoing vows needs three judges, so one judge cannot do it.

steps.title: Maybe the case is a court of three
steps.stepSummary: Since one judge cannot undo vows, the גמרא suggests the משנה means three judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is with three judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to read the משנה: the vow was brought before three judges. This is only a setup, and the very next line attacks it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 ruled out one judge, because undoing vows needs three. So the natural next try is a court of three. The problem is whether three judges would be suspected at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (offering a new suggestion after the last one failed)

phrases.english: Rather, with three.
phrases.notes: He means three judges handled the woman's נדר and refused to undo it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected one-judge reading with a three-judge reading
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Could the משנה be talking about a court of three judges?

steps.title: A court of three is not suspected
steps.stepSummary: The משנה itself says a judge in a court of three may marry the woman, so three judges are not suspected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are three judges suspected? But we learned in the משנה: if she did מיאון or חליצה before him, he may marry her, because he was one of a court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the three-judge reading. It points out that the same משנה trusts a judge who sat on a court of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets a judge marry a woman whose מיאון or חליצה he saw, because he was one of a בית דין of three. That shows a court of three is not suspected of bending the law for itself. So the חכם who is forbidden to marry her cannot be one of three judges either.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they suspected? (of acting for their own benefit)
But didn't we learn (in a משנה)?
Refusal: a girl married off as a minor by her mother or brothers leaves the marriage by refusing
The ceremony that frees a childless widow from יבום

phrases.english: Are they suspect?
But didn't we learn:
If she refused or did חליצה before him,
phrases.notes: This is the same משנה we saw back in step 14.

phrases.english: he may marry her, because he is a court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the three-judge suggestion of step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the forbidden חכם was one of three judges
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says a judge in a court of three is not suspected, so a three-judge case would not lead to a ban on marrying her

steps.title: The case is a single expert judge
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means one judge who is an expert, since an expert may undo vows alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it is one judge, as רב חסדא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: vows can be undone by a single expert. Here too, it means a single expert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the one-judge reading, but says the judge is an expert. An expert is allowed to undo vows by himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17's problem was that an ordinary person alone cannot undo vows. But רבי יוחנן says a יחיד מומחה can. Since he acts alone and not as part of a court, he can be suspected, so he may not marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (going back to the first idea)

steps.whatToRemember: The חכם in the משנה who may not marry the woman is a יחיד מומחה, a single expert who can undo vows alone. A judge in a court of three is not suspected.

phrases.english: Actually, with one,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִדְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and as Rav Ḥisda said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
by a single expert,
here too: by a single expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בְּחַד, וְכִדְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers steps 17 and 19 by bringing back the one-judge reading with an expert
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case more narrowly: a single expert
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One judge cannot undo vows, and three are not suspected, so the case seemed impossible
steps.terutzMaskana: A single expert can undo vows alone, and since he acts alone he is suspected

steps.title: Only a full court is trusted, not two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה closely: the reason is that he was a court, so with only two judges he could not marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: She refused or did חליצה, etc. The reason is that it was a court, so with two it would not be allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the line about מיאון and חליצה and draws a lesson from its wording. This sets up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the reason 'because he is a court', which means three. So the גמרא learns that if only two judges were present, he would be suspected and could not marry her.

phrases.english: She refused or did חליצה, etc.
The reason is because it was a court,
but with two, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּבֵית דִּין, הָא בִּתְרֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic by reading the מיאון line of the משנה closely
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the משנה relies on a full court, it seems that with only two judges he could not marry her

steps.title: But two witnesses are not suspected
steps.stepSummary: Witnesses who sign a sale or a גט may later buy the field or marry the woman, so why would two judges be suspected?
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from what we learned: witnesses who signed on the sale of a field or on a woman's גט, the חכמים were not concerned about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the lesson from step 21. Elsewhere, just two witnesses are trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A witness who signed a sale document may later buy that field, and a witness who signed a גט may later marry that woman. The חכמים were not worried, because two people would not plot together to help one of them. So two judges should also not be suspected.

phrases.english: What is different from that which we learned:
witnesses signed on a field's sale,
or on a woman's גט,
the Sages were not concerned about this matter?
phrases.notes: 'This matter' means a witness later buying that field or marrying that woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lesson drawn in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that two judges would be suspected
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two signing witnesses are not suspected of helping one of themselves, so two judges should not be suspected either

steps.title: The point is that מיאון needs three
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions a court not because two are suspected, but to teach that מיאון must be done before three.
steps.simpleTranslation: That itself is what it teaches us: to reject the one who says מיאון can be before two. It teaches us that מיאון needs three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that two judges really are not suspected. The משנה says 'court' to teach how many people מיאון needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lesson in step 21 is dropped: the word 'court' is not about suspicion. It tells us that מיאון must be done before three, against the opinion that two are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: That itself is what it comes to teach us

steps.whatToRemember: Two judges or witnesses are not suspected of acting for themselves. The משנה says 'court' to teach that מיאון must be done before three.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'court' is not saying two judges are suspected. It is teaching the rule for how מיאון must be done.

phrases.english: That itself is what it teaches us,
to exclude the one who says
refusal is before two,
it teaches us refusal is with three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 by giving the word 'court' a different purpose
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the wording a new purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'court' seemed to mean that two judges would be suspected
steps.terutzMaskana: Two are not suspected; the משנה says 'court' to teach that מיאון needs three
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the rule that מיאון must be done before a court of three, rejecting the view that two are enough.

steps.title: If he married her anyway, must he divorce her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a man who married a woman he was not supposed to marry must divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if he married her, does he have to divorce her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. A man was told he should not marry a certain woman, but he married her anyway. Does he now have to divorce her?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about who may or may not marry a woman in the first place (לכתחילה). Now the גמרא asks about after the fact (בדיעבד): once the marriage has already happened, do we undo it?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (the חכמים)
Literally 'takes out'; here it means he must divorce her

steps.confusionAlert: This is not asking whether he may marry her. Everyone agrees he should not. The question is only what happens after he already did.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
If he married her, what is the law, must he divorce her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether he may marry her to what happens after he already married her.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a marriage that should not have happened must be ended by divorce.

steps.title: רב כהנא says he must divorce her
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rules that if he married her, he must divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: if he married her, he must divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives the first answer: the marriage cannot stay, so he must divorce her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב כהנא's view, the rule against marrying her still applies after the wedding. So we undo the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who holds he must divorce her

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: If he married her, he must divorce her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question.

steps.title: רב אשי says he does not need to divorce her
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי disagrees and rules that if he married her, he does not have to divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: if he married her, he does not need to divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the opposite answer: once the marriage has happened, it can stay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אשי, the rule is only meant to stop the marriage from happening. Once it has already happened, we do not force a divorce. This sets up a clear מחלוקת with רב כהנא.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who holds he does not need to divorce her
He does not need to divorce her

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כָּנַס — אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא.
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: If he married her, he need not divorce her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב כהנא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He does not need to divorce her.

steps.title: רב זוטי teaches a source that agrees with רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטי from the school of רב פפי taught a teaching that matches רב אשי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטי of the school of רב פפי taught them in line with the one who says that if he married her, he does not need to divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זוטי brings a teaching (a ברייתא) that supports רב אשי's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds an outside source behind רב אשי. Now his view is not just one opinion in a מחלוקת; a taught source agrees with it.

keyTerms.meaning: רב זוטי from the study hall of רב פפי
In line with the words of the one who says

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי לְהוּ רַב זוּטֵי דְּבֵי רַב פַּפֵּי
phrases.english: Rav Zuti of the school of Rav Pappi taught them
in accordance with the one who says: if he married her, he need not divorce her.
phrases.notes: That's רב אשי's view from the step before.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי לְהוּ רַב זוּטֵי דְּבֵי רַב פַּפֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's ruling with a taught source.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's ruling that he does not need to divorce her
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רב זוטי of the school of רב פפי

steps.title: The חכמים ask רב אשי where his ruling comes from
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רב אשי whether his ruling comes from a tradition he received or from his own reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said to רב אשי: is this a tradition, or your own reasoning?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask רב אשי for the source of his view. Did a teacher hand it down to him, or did he work it out himself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: גמרא here means a tradition received from teachers, and סברא means one's own logic. A received tradition would carry more weight than personal reasoning, so the answer matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a tradition received from one's teachers

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גמרא does not mean the Talmud. It means a teaching handed down from one's teachers.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rav Ashi:
Is it a received tradition, or reasoning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of רב אשי's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב אשי's ruling is a received tradition or his own reasoning.

steps.title: רב אשי answers: it comes from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says his source is the משנה about a man suspected with a שפחה or a גויה: he should not marry her, but if he did, they do not take her away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: it is a משנה. A man suspected with a שפחה who was later freed, or with a גויה who later converted, should not marry her. But if he did marry her, they do not take her away from him. Apparently...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows that his ruling comes from the משנה. He quotes it and begins to draw his proof with the word אלמא ('apparently'), which sets up the conclusion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly separates 'he should not marry her' (לכתחילה) from 'if he married, we do not remove her' (בדיעבד). That is exactly רב אשי's position. The word אלמא shows he is about to state the general rule he learns from this case.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי learns from the משנה's words 'ואם כנס אין מוציא' that once he has married her, we do not force a divorce, even though he should not have married her to begin with.

phrases.english: He said to them: It is the mishna:
One suspected with a maidservant who was then freed,
or with a gentile woman who then converted —
this man may not marry her,
but if he did marry her, they do not remove her.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the court. The judges do not take her away from him.

phrases.english: Apparently,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' question by pointing to the משנה as the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling comes from the משנה's words 'ואם כנס אין מוציא'.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's ruling that he does not need to divorce her
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about one suspected with a שפחה or a גויה
